value.first: At 6 months he's right on time. I'd use iron-first solids with early allergen introduction, because the iron he banked before birth runs low now, and eating allergens early and often cuts allergy risk (LEAP trial: about 80% less peanut allergy in high-risk babies). Day 1: upright in the high chair, a rested, slightly hungry moment, a spoon or two of iron-fortified oat cereal or puréed beef. Days 2-7: iron-rich food twice a day plus veg and fruit. Milk stays the same.
value.second: Week 2, peanut first: in the morning, thin half a teaspoon of smooth peanut butter with warm water or breast milk, never a glob. Give a taste, wait 10 minutes, then feed the rest and watch him for 2 hours, no other new foods. Next day or so: well-cooked egg, same routine. Then one new allergen a day: yogurt, wheat, tofu, tahini, thinned nut butters, flaked fish. Once tolerated, serve each about twice a week. Dropping one can undo the protection.
value.third: Gagging is noisy and normal. Choking is silent. Refusal is normal too, so retry another day. No honey, whole nuts, whole grapes or cow milk as a drink yet. Hives, vomiting or a rash from a food: stop it and see your doctor. Trouble breathing, swelling or going floppy is an emergency. If you'd rather skip purees, baby-led finger foods work too, same allergen plan. I'll check in Thursday.
